long_biography.plain_text:
At Gaming and Leisure Properties, Peter M. Carlino directs a landlord rather than a casino operator. The company acquires, finances and owns properties leased to gaming businesses under long-term arrangements. His economic exposure comes through disclosed GLPI equity, both directly and through trust-linked interests; the individual properties remain corporate holdings, not personal ones. This distinction also marks the change in Carlino's career after 2013: property capital and tenant relationships replaced day-to-day casino operations as his principal public-company remit.

The institutional roots are familial. Peter D. Carlino established the Pennsylvania racing enterprise from which the later companies developed, while his son shaped strategy across the family holding company from the 1970s onward. Carlino now remains PENN chairman emeritus, not its operating chief, alongside his active leadership at GLPI. He has also served Penn State Health and supported an inflammatory-bowel-disease centre combining clinical care, education and research.
